card: Reject wallet names composed exclusively of whitespace characters across RPC wallet creation, wallet dumping, and bitcoin-wallet tool operations. Bitcoin Core currently forbids empty-string wallet names but allows whitespace-only names, which create confusing and practically nameless directories on the filesystem. The author demonstrates that commands like `bitcoin-cli createwallet "    "` currently succeed and generate visually ambiguous directory names.
evidence: The author demonstrates in the PR description that `bitcoin-cli createwallet "                            "` succeeds, producing filesystem entries like `'                        '` under the wallets directory.
problem: Bitcoin Core disallows empty string wallet names, but permits wallet names composed entirely of whitespace characters (e.g., spaces). Such names create filesystem directories that are confusing or indistinguishable from nameless paths to users.
summary: Reject wallet creation when the specified wallet name consists solely of whitespace characters. The empty-name validation in `CreateWallet`, `CreateFromDump`, and `bitcoin-wallet create` checks whether trimming the name results in an empty string view, without modifying the underlying name string if valid.
